analyst_note: Hormuz Day 113 — MOU In Force, Nuclear 60-Day Clock Day 1: The June 19 digital signing of the US-Iran MOU is the decisive close of the longest open-ended geopolitical overhang tracked in this series. The Strait of Hormuz blockade enters its formal dissolution phase: the MOU is legally operative, the nuclear 60-day negotiation window has activated, and the oil sanctions waiver is live. The Geneva physical ceremony was cancelled due to Lebanon overnight violence on June 19; the digital signing format carried full legal effect and both principals confirmed completion. Hormuz blockade dissolution enters Day 6. First commercial tanker transits are underway — 18 transits recorded across the June 17-18 window, predominantly Chinese-affiliated vessels as first movers, with European, Japanese, and Saudi tonnage among the early departures. Shipping normalization remains on a 2-4 week timeline to full commercial reintegration. WTI closed Thursday at approximately $74 per barrel. The critical upcoming inflection: Monday June 22 — the first US market session after both Juneteenth closure and confirmed MOU signing. Monday open prices the signed deal into equities, fixed income, and commodities for the first time with legal certainty. FOMC hawkish dot-plot overhang (9 hike dots, Dow -507, 2-year +16bps from June 17 Warsh presser) processes in a deal-signed context; the energy-CPI gap between the dot's implicit $95-100 oil assumption and the post-deal WTI trajectory will be the primary market narrative heading into September's first post-deal SEP. In the Pacific Northwest: Upriver Fire enters Day 4 with fatality now formally confirmed — the 2026 season's first wildfire death. Overnight conditions were favorable (cool stable air mass, low winds) and first-morning NIFC updates expected to show significant containment improvement from the 10% Day-3 baseline; overnight reports indicate 30%+ advance. Evacuation levels continued downgrading Saturday morning for Spokane Valley sectors. Juniper Dunes (~10,577 acres) and Twin Sisters (~8,262 acres) enter Day 2 of the post-heat containment window. Reconciliation 2.0: Speaker Johnson's July 2 floor date signal puts the legislative calendar at T-12 from today. Freedom Caucus outstanding issues — spending caps, Medicaid work requirements, anti-weaponization provisions — remain the binding constraint. Measles dual incubation windows active: Day 6 from the June 15 Lumen Field match (cluster ID window June 22-29) and Day 2 from the June 19 match (window through July 3). CIDRAP slowing signal Day 14. CISA Day 50 clean — post-signing Shamkhani cyber window shifts from pre-signing disruption motivation to post-signing retaliation opportunism (lower probability envelope). NSF Newport OR ocean observatories approximately 8 days from removal. East Cascades wildfire onset approximately T-9. Saturday, June 20, 2026. MOU Day 1. Nuclear 60-Day Clock Day 1. WTI ~$74 recovering. CISA Day 50 clean. Measles 2,073 (CDC June 11). WPA Day 112 moot.

The Juneteenth market closure and weekend position provide a two-day buffer before Monday June 22 — the first session where investors can price the signed deal with legal certainty. Primary negative signals: Upriver Fire confirmed fatality (2026 PNW season first, elevates domestic emergency to mass-casualty federal threshold) and dual measles incubation windows (two concurrent Lumen Field exposure events running through July 3). No systemic downside triggers active: CISA Day 50 clean, Shamkhani window shifts to lower-probability post-signing envelope, Iranian MOU repudiation signal absent, G7 allied alignment holds. Upside to 7: Monday June 22 markets open strongly on signed deal + tanker traffic normalizing + no IRGC post-signing cyber incident. Downside to 5: IRGC post-signing cyber retaliation confirmed; measles cluster emergence from Lumen Field events; Iranian public MOU compliance objection; Reconciliation 2.0 Freedom Caucus walkout.

items.summary: The June 19 digital signing of the US-Iran MOU closes the primary open geopolitical variable of the 2026 Iran conflict arc. Both principals confirmed electronic signing on June 19, conferring full legal effect. The Geneva physical ceremony was cancelled due to Lebanon overnight violence in the pre-dawn hours of June 19 — emerging after all three Lebanon Quiet Day performance tests had been cleared (Day 3 cleared ~8 PM PDT June 18). The digital signing format was the pre-agreed operative fallback; it was executed and is binding. Key MOU architecture entering Day 1: (1) Nuclear 60-day negotiation window activated — clock runs June 19 to approximately August 17. Deliverables: Iranian HEU removal timetable, enrichment suspension parameters, verification framework, permanent sanctions architecture. (2) Oil sanctions waiver live — Iranian oil re-entry into global markets on a 3-6 week timeline from signing. (3) Paragraph 5 commercial transit: charge-free transit between the Persian Gulf and Sea of Oman for 60 days, demining within 30 days. (4) CENTCOM blockade dissolution Day 6. First commercial tanker transits underway: Windward AI and CNBC reporting 18 transits across the June 17-18 window. Five of seven documented first movers Chinese-affiliated; European, Japanese, and Saudi tonnage among early departures. Shipping companies and insurance underwriters have not fully resumed normal tariff structures — signed MOU is the commercial trigger for underwriter normalization, 2-4 weeks. WTI approximately $74 pre-market June 20. The Monday June 22 US market open is the operative pricing session for the signed deal.

items.summary: Four secondary geopolitical threads entering June 20 morning. First: CISA advances to Day 50 clean streak. The Shamkhani cyber threat window shifts character at signing: the pre-signing window (Days 1-26) carried peak disruption motivation — IRGC cyber actors could justify last-ditch infrastructure disruption to derail the deal. Post-signing (Day 27+), the profile shifts to retaliation opportunism — lower probability but not zero, as hardline IRGC factions may seek to register objection to the MOU's nuclear terms. CISA Day 50 clean is the operative counter-indicator. Second: G7 allied alignment confirmed at Évian summit June 15-17 and held through the signing-day Lebanon disruption — remains operative entering Day 1 post-signing. Third: WPA Day 112, 22 days past the hard 90-day constitutional deadline, fully moot. The deal-era resolution renders the War Powers Act debate structurally closed; four Senate enforcement blocks and House 215-208 vote are locked precedent. Fourth: Acting DNI vacancy enters Day 30 at the post-signing IC verification load — the 60-day nuclear clock demands ongoing intelligence community verification of Iranian HEU inventory, enrichment status, and IRGC stand-down compliance. Day 30 is the first day of the nuclear window's active verification requirements.

items.summary: Two secondary economic threads. First: following the June 18 FERC Section 206 show cause orders issued bipartisan 5-0 to PJM, MISO, SPP, CAISO, ISO-NE, and NYISO, the response period is now active. Saturday is an analytical quiet window; first substantive grid operator responses expected week of June 22. Key outstanding questions: how aggressively PJM and MISO challenge the cost allocation framework (large loads bearing interconnection upgrade costs rather than socializing to ratepayers), and how quickly hyperscalers with pending Pacific Northwest interconnection requests respond to changed economics. BPA's drought-year-4 constrained hydropower position remains relevant context for Northwest grid absorptive capacity. Second: Reconciliation 2.0 enters the weekend at T-12 to Speaker Johnson's July 2 floor date signal (issued June 19 evening). No floor action expected Saturday. Freedom Caucus outstanding demands — spending caps at Biden-era versus pre-Biden baselines, Medicaid work requirements framework, anti-weaponization provisions — remain unresolved. Iran deal signing eliminates FC war-cost leverage but does not dissolve FC substantive policy demands. The week of June 22 is the critical conversion window for Johnson's July 2 signal to a confirmed House Rules Committee scheduling action.

items.summary: The Upriver Fire northeast of Spokane enters Day 4 with its status materially improved from June 19 morning on one critical and one positive dimension. Critical: the wildfire fatality is now formally confirmed. Human remains recovered June 18 from a burned structure on Upriver Drive have been identified — the individual refused to evacuate during the fire's June 17 wind-driven run, with family members calling law enforcement and deputies conducting repeated door-to-door warnings before the fire consumed the structure. This is the 2026 Pacific Northwest wildfire season's first confirmed wildfire death. Governor Ferguson's FEMA fire management assistance declaration request gains additional weight from the confirmed fatality. Positive: overnight suppression conditions were favorable — cool stable post-frontal air mass, low winds, recovering humidity. Initial morning reports indicate containment has advanced significantly from the 10% Day-3 baseline, with indicators in the 30-60% range. The NIFC morning daily update (~6-8 AM PDT) will provide the first authoritative figure. Evacuation levels continuing to downgrade for Spokane Valley sectors — Level 3 zones transitioning to Level 2 and Level 1 in some areas as fire perimeter stabilizes. Approximately 300 personnel active. The Upriver Fire's WUI character and confirmed fatality carry outsized public visibility relative to its ~350-acre footprint.
